## Repository findings

- **No game or app source currently exists at the repository root.** There is no root `index.html`, `package.json`, Vite config, or app JS/CSS/React source. The root file search returned no app entry files.
- **The existing startup script is an environment launcher, not a game entry point:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/start.sh` runs the platform’s `default-start.mjs` via `$RUNTIME_DIR`. `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/startup.sh` is only a shell stub.
- **Supported app formats:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.omgithub/scripts/default-start.mjs` serves a plain static project when it has `index.html`, or builds and serves a Vite project. It explicitly rejects Next.js and other package projects without a custom startup/deployment setup.
- **Deployment guidance:** `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.omgithub/.github/prompts/02-verify.md` calls for repeatable startup, static output, and desktop/mobile capture. The default capture runner checks a 1440×900 desktop viewport and a 390×844 mobile viewport: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.omgithub/scripts/default-capture.mjs`.
- **The only existing HTML/CSS/JS example is an infrastructure fixture**, not part of the app: `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/.omgithub/.github/fixtures/test-project/`. Its `index.html`, `app.js`, and `styles.css` illustrate a small static project, but do not provide a game framework.

## Recommendation

Build the game as a small **static browser app**, either with plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript or Vite; there is no existing framework to extend. A good implementation structure would separate the game UI from a deterministic simulation engine, with challenge data and validation rules kept in their own modules.

For the core loop, give the player a code editor or command console, a visible simulated machine/world, and a clear objective. Let players run, step, pause, and reset their programs; show output, errors, and useful state/debug information. A small, purpose-built instruction language is safer and easier to validate than executing arbitrary player-entered JavaScript. Include a tutorial and several progressively harder challenges so the result is playable beyond a single demo interaction.

Keep the interface responsive and ensure the editor, simulation, and controls remain usable on mobile, consistent with `/home/runner/work/PlayGround/PlayGround/Agents.md`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable computer simulation game where the player programs a machine using an invented language.

## Requirements
- Deliver a playable game without clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Check the result with small JPEG screenshots (viewport no wider than 1280px); inspect only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Implemented a static browser game called Machine Room, with the custom SPARK language and a tile-based robot simulation.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the responsive game UI, SPARK language guide, mission selector, editor, live grid, controls, and system log.
- Added four missions and a bounded parser/interpreter supporting movement, turns, cell pickup, conditionals, and repeats.
- Verified `game.js` syntax and exercised mission 1 to completion and mission 2 in the browser.
- Saved and inspected `/tmp/opencode/machine-room.jpg`.

### Active
- Finish browser validation, including mission completion and mobile layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser checks for all missions, parser errors, and mobile layout.
2. Check the latest edits, including the favicon change; run `node --check game.js` and inspect the latest screenshot.
3. Summarize implementation and validation results.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game page structure and SPARK guide.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design.
- `game.js`: Mission data, SPARK parser/interpreter, simulation, and controls.

## Important Context
- Mission 1 completed successfully in-browser; mission 2 was running and had collected its cell when last checked.
- The files are uncommitted.
